note: Append-only activity log. The verification pipeline writes an entry for every field-level change it makes; humans write entries for decisions. This is what the /updates page renders, and it is the audit trail that makes an autonomous board trustworthy.

kinds.changed: A tracked field changed on an existing entry
kinds.verified: Confidence moved up: a claim got corroborated or confirmed
kinds.missed: A deadline passed without us acting

updates.title: Discovery sweep: three new entries, and the reason nothing new was showing up
updates.body: The complaint that prompted this sweep was 'no new opportunities', and the cause turned out to be structural rather than a dry market. Zindi was carried as a single row called 'Zindi Challenges (rolling)' with status monitor-weekly and no dates at all. A row with no next_date never appears in any deadline view, so five live Zindi competitions were invisible, including R.O.A.D. Barbados Historic Handwriting at $25,000 which opened on 3 July and had been running for seven weeks. Promoted the two worth entering to real dated rows: R.O.A.D. Barbados ($25,000, closes 5 Oct, OCR on degraded historic scans, the best skills match on the board) and Bias Bounty Mapping Equity ($10,000, opens 28 Aug, closes 1 Nov, geospatial). The other three are recorded inside the rolling row rather than promoted: the ITU drought challenge is EUR 2,000 with 430 already active and collides with the Shipaton sprint, and the remaining two are $1,000 and points-only. Rule going forward: a rolling source is a pointer to where competitions live, never a substitute for the competitions themselves.

updates.title: Nedbank N*ovation added as a monitor: 50 seats is the best field size found anywhere
updates.body: Found at apply.hackathon.nedbank.co.za, which still advertises the 2025 edition with applications closed 31 Oct 2025. No 2026 dates exist, so none were recorded and none were invented. Added anyway because the shape is unusually good: capped at 50 participants, R300,000 in prizes across the top three, and direct exposure to Nedbank tech leadership, which is the highest career leverage per hour of anything local found so far. Two honest discounts applied rather than glossed: prizes are AVO vouchers not cash, so the prize sub-score is 6 not 8, and the 2025 brief asks for 'senior and experienced technologists', which for a two-graduate team is a real eligibility risk, so winnability is 6 not 8. That question should be asked of Nedbank directly rather than assumed in either direction. Diarised as a monthly check from 1 Sept: a 50-seat event is lost by missing the announcement, not by losing the contest.

updates.title: Four candidates checked and rejected, with reasons, plus three new monitoring sources
updates.body: Recorded so the same ground is not re-walked next week. USAII Global AI Hackathon 2026: dead, not open. The search result read as live but the Devpost page shows registration expired 6 June and the event ran 14 to 22 June. Cyber AI Hackathon 2026 (theamse.org): real dates, 31 Oct to 1 Nov at the University of Derby, but in-person UK, only $1,600, and the organiser contact is a gmail address with a phone number embedded in it, which is a credibility smell on a body calling itself the American Society for Engineers. Rejected. Nedbank Data Masters Challenge 2026: confirmed past, registration closed end April. DIRISA Student Datathon (CSIR): genuinely well-targeted at SA students and graduates, but the programme page still reads 'SDC 2025' and 'more information to be confirmed', so there is nothing to enter. Added to sources on a monthly cadence instead. Also added HackOn (SA community series, nothing scheduled) and Nedbank. Worth noting for calibration: dev.events lists ZERO in-person hackathons anywhere in Africa from September 2026 onward, so the thin local pipeline is real and not a monitoring failure.

updates.title: Monday sweep: Geekulcha's real dates found, and the deadline is tomorrow
updates.body: The entry had been carrying an 'expected_window' of September to October and no deadline at all, on the reasoning that the team dashboard showed no date. The organiser's own registration platform states them plainly: concept pack due 25 Aug 2026 23:59, hackathon 25 to 27 September in Centurion with a virtual option, build-up webinars 8 to 17 September. That puts the deadline one day out, not one month, which retrospectively explains the 20 Aug dashboard reading where 8 of 9 documents landed within hours of each other. The urgency sub-score of 9 was already right for the wrong reason. Lesson worth keeping: the dashboard shows what we submitted, the event page shows what is required, and only the second one carries dates. Checking the team dashboard is not the same as checking the source.

updates.title: Possible eligibility problem recorded against MoMo, deliberately not acted on
updates.body: Secondary sources describe an MTN Group '3rd MoMo Open API Hackathon' with an idea phase of 21 Oct to 8 Dec 2026, open only to Ghana, Uganda, Cote d'Ivoire, Cameroon and Zambia. If that is this contest under another name then the entry's 'Multi-country incl. South Africa' location is wrong and the team is not eligible at all. It has not been treated as fact and nothing was downgraded: the team submitted first-hand on 16 Aug, which no search result outranks, and 'MoMo Mini App' has never been shown to be the same programme as 'MoMo Open API'. Filed under dates.possible_related_programme so the question is visible rather than lost, and resolvable the only way it can be, by reading the confirmation email.

updates.title: Calendar reconciled against the board: seven events missing, two stale

Added: Geekulcha's 25 Aug deadline and 25 to 27 Sept event, the Mintek final hacking day on 1 Oct and the mandatory SCI Conference on 2 Oct, the SME Toolkit final business plan on 30 Nov, the GovTech awards on 23 Sept, and W3Node in November. The two Mintek entries and the SME Toolkit deadline were the serious omissions: all three are hard commitments, and one is an in-person day with a 13:00 code cutoff. Corrected two stale entries: the ADTC submission alarm was still set to fire today for a competition dropped on 16 Aug, now relabelled and freed rather than deleted so the decision stays on the record, and GovTech still read 'VERIFY ELIGIBILITY' when eligibility was resolved and the in-person track chosen a week ago.

updates.title: Winnability reevaluated across the board; one change, one bug found
updates.body: Standing practice: recheck every entry's chances rather than letting a scored guess sit untouched. Changed exactly one. Mintek winnability 7 to 8, because the team has since cleared a competitive selection gate confirmed by letter, so the odds of a top-3 finish are genuinely better than when the row was scored as a mere applicant. Everything else was reviewed and held: two recorded outcomes is far too thin to start moving numbers on, and the Entelect result mostly confirms the existing calibration rather than contradicting it. Separately this pass uncovered a real bug: score is the weighted sum of the sub-scores for all 19 entries, but Mintek stored 8.2 against a true 7.65, so its rank on the board had been overstated since the selection update. Corrected to 7.95 and migrate_to_opportunities.py now warns whenever a stored score and its sub-scores disagree.

updates.title: Entelect University Cup 2: competed, ~10th at leaderboard freeze
updates.body: Result recorded from the team's own engineering log (Entelect-Optimisation-Challenge/HANDOVER.md), which is now the authoritative record. Shipped and portal-verified 121,860,709 across four levels (15,358,600 / 21,090,840 / 36,984,815 / 48,426,454). Leaderboard froze with the team around 10th at 120,444,763 against a #1 of 125,270,208: 3.85% behind at freeze, final shipped total 97.28% of the leader. Placing is deliberately recorded as unconfirmed: Entelect closed the leaderboard after the event and retains no score history, so this is the last observed standing, not a certified rank. Status moved to past, lifecycle to judged, and the entry moved into the archive.

updates.title: Playbook: sourced research on how these competitions actually get won
updates.body: Added a Playbook to the landing page. Every claim carries a named source and a link, and the entries are split by phase (before / during / after) and by competition type, because leaderboard-scored contests and judged pitch events reward different behaviour and blending them produces advice that is wrong for both. Includes the team's own measured evidence from the Entelect Cup alongside external research, marked as such.

updates.title: Geekulcha #GKHack26 - submitted, confirmed first-hand via team dashboard

Score 5.45->5.75, still tier 3.

updates.title: SME Toolkit SA Business Plan Competition — Phase 1 submitted, 2 individual entries
updates.body: Reported first-hand: Phase 1 submitted 18 Aug 2026, 13 days ahead of the 31 Aug close. status open -> submitted, lifecycle scored -> submitted. TWO separate individual entries, not one team submission — SME Toolkit's eligibility is per-person: Sibusiso with Karoo Compute (shared GPU/AI compute infrastructure for South Africa), Lethabo with Indlela AI (agentic-AI engineering studio). Both plans' full content — problem, business model, numbers — recorded in what_to_build; both already have a full multi-page business plan and a live five-year financial model. Score recalculated, not left stale: urgency sub-score 9 -> 4 now that the imminent Phase 1 deadline is done and the next real gate is the 30 Nov business plan (104 days out), calibrated against the board's own precedent (RSNA at 59 days scores urgency 7, NASA at 89 days scores urgency 5). Composite score 5.75 -> 5.0, still Tier 3, argued in the PR per Standing Agreement 8, not changed silently. Housekeeping: the now-fulfilled registration_deadline was renamed to phase1_close_date (a key scripts/sonar.py's DEADLINE_KEYS won't rank on) and a new phase1_entered_on fact added — same pattern mintek-sci-2026 already uses for team_notified alongside a still-live submission_deadline. Confirmed via `sonar.py list`: next date now correctly reads 30 Nov / 104 days, not the completed 31 Aug one.

updates.title: Weekly discovery sweep — 3 new opportunities added, local-priority
updates.body: Manual Tier A/B-style sweep (docs/AUTONOMY.md §4), local priority per instruction, international welcome. ~25 searches and direct fetches. 3 added, all Tier 3: sme-toolkit-business-plan-2026 (score 5.75, Phase 1 closes 31 Aug — 14 days out), w3node-hackathon-2026 (score 4.6, Cape Town, 12-14 Nov), ai-infra-summit-hackathon-2026 (score 4.25, Santa Clara CA, online track only). Full source citations in docs/SOURCES.md's new 'Discovery sweep' section, including everything checked and rejected with a reason — 5 real events already past their 2026 date (Nedbank Data Masters, Deep Learning Indaba + IndabaX SA, 2x Hack-Nation cycles, Microsoft AI Dev Days) and 5 rejected on sourcing/fit (AfriHack — no primary-sourced date; CyberSecureTech — 2026 edition not yet scheduled; WeThinkCode x Base — the event's OWN page says 2025, an aggregator got the year wrong; IBM Bob 2.0 on lablab.ai — two mutually exclusive dates, page 403'd on direct fetch, neither confirmed; Hack the North — student-only and likely already closed). Two housekeeping fixes made in the same pass: the new entries' date keys were renamed to match scripts/sonar.py's recognised DEADLINE_KEYS list (registration_deadline/final_submission/event_start) after the CLI silently failed to rank them under custom key names — caught by re-running `sonar.py next`/`list` after adding, not by inspection. And PRIORITY_BOARD.md's ADTC row still said 'Open' despite data/opportunities.json already marking it dropped (NOT COMPETING, decided 16 Aug, by another session) — fixed the one cell while already editing that table.

updates.title: SITA GovTech 2026 — EME entity registered, eligibility blocker cleared
updates.body: Reported first-hand: the EME/SMME entity registration required by T&Cs 2.1 is done. Combined with the team now being three (2.2), both halves of the blocker recorded on 10 Aug are cleared. Entity name and registration date are not supplied and are NOT recorded here — fill in when to hand rather than guessed. Also: read the full T&Cs PDF for the first time (govtech.gov.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/GovTech-2026-Hackathon-Terms-and-Condition.pdf) rather than relying on the earlier summary. Upgrades dates.confidence reported -> confirmed, since the 17-19 Sept dates are now read directly off the primary source (T&Cs 2.3), not a secondary one. New facts captured: winners announced 23 Sept at an Awards Ceremony, distinct from the event itself; only one team per company may register (1.2) — worth checking the registered entity hasn't fielded another team; prize money (if any is won) is taxable and paid 30 days after the event; SITA takes an irrevocable worldwide license over Hackathon Outputs, though pre-existing 'Background IP' stays ours if flagged before or at time of use — worth doing explicitly given REEFPRINT-style reuse across entries.

updates.title: MTN MoMo Mini App Hackathon: submitted, three ideas, three-person team
updates.body: Reported first-hand by an operator. Status monitor → submitted, lifecycle triaged → submitted. The team entered THREE separate ideas under one team rather than a single joint entry: three shots on goal. Worth confirming against MTN's rules that multiple submissions per team are permitted and judged independently. Deliberately NOT recorded, because they were not supplied and this board does not guess: the submission date, the three idea titles, and the third member's identity. confidence stays unconfirmed and next_date stays null: no 2026 MTN date has been read off a source yet. KNOCK-ON: the team is now three people. docs/TEAM.md describes a two-person team throughout, and Standing Agreement 1 (max two overlapping builds) is sized for two. More concretely, govtech-2026's team_fit reads 'Needs a 3rd (and possibly 4th/5th) member AND a registered entity': the team-size half of that blocker is now cleared on an entry scoring 6.45, higher than MTN's own 6.2, which was otherwise heading for a drop. The EME/SMME entity requirement is still unresolved and GovTech runs 17-19 Sept.

updates.title: Fixed a fabricated-outcome bug: 5 events wrongly shown as "entered"

Five entries were just discovery notes ("ran on X date, diarise for next year") we never actually applied to: ITWeb Security Summit Hackathon, MICT SETA National Skills Challenge, Monkey and River Hackathon, GirlCode Pan-African Hackathon, Geekulcha SS26Hack Kimberley: and the site was showing all five as things the team entered. updates.title: UNESCO Youth Hackathon 2026: submitted
updates.body: Submitted HAYIBO: an interactive toolkit teaching South Africans, especially digitally illiterate and older audiences, to spot AI deepfakes and misinformation the way it actually spreads locally (WhatsApp voice notes, Facebook, radio call-in), via five spoken verification questions that need no reading or device. Taught through a weekly two-clip real-vs-AI guessing game run simultaneously on WhatsApp, Facebook (public leaderboard) and community radio (elders phone in and reason aloud). Every round is logged by language and platform and published openly: the first public dataset of AI-generated misinformation in isiZulu, Sepedi and other SA languages. Deliverables sent: proposal document, 9-slide pitch deck, 2:57 narrated video pitch. Confirmation email received; results expected mid-September 2026. Status moved to submitted.

updates.title: Mintek-SCi Grad Hackathon 2026: REEFPRINT abstract recorded
updates.body: Added the submitted abstract to what_to_build: REEFPRINT (Problem 3: Computer Vision for Real-Time Mineralogical Characterisation), by Lethabo. Distills SEM/XRD/QEMSCAN output into a fast optical model across five Bushveld phases, reports per-class recall on sub-1% base-metal sulphide ahead of aggregate accuracy, converts texture into liberation/reagent demand/grindability with calibrated abstention, costs in Rand/tCO2e, and is positioned as a StarCS/FloatStar/MillStar module.

updates.title: ADTC prize conflict closed: arithmetic confirms the earlier ruling
updates.body: Press reported "$20,000+" against Devpost's itemised $16,500. Confirmed by arithmetic that both are correct and describe different things: 8000+4000+3000+1500 = $16,500 cash, and 10×$250 + 20×$50 = $3,500 in GPU credits, totalling exactly $20,000. No action needed.

The board models this as a single submit-once deadline. Keeping Devpost's earlier date, since submitting early is free, but flagged for a manual check of the organiser page before the 24th.
